answer: Agents anchor identity in a shared ocean of locked stake: each deposits tokens in a shared pool, lost on proven Sybil behavior. Reputation works like a prism, splitting each record into facets — uptime, task accuracy, peer endorsements — so a fake must counterfeit all facets. One thread of attestations links an agent's actions across epochs; forking a second thread restarts the clock, and thread age is public. Creating N fakes costs N stakes, N threads of real work, and N prisms, while rewards per identity stay flat — so Sybil scale is irrational.
